articles.title: International Support Is Not a Country Dropdown
articles.excerpt: "Our form accepts addresses from around the world" is a sentence that appears in a lot of product copy and survives in very few codebases. International support usually means a US address form with a…
articles.body: "Our form accepts addresses from around the world" is a sentence that appears in a lot of product copy and survives in very few codebases. International support usually means a US address form with a country dropdown added at the end — and a validation stack that still assumes every address has a five-digit ZIP, a two-letter state and a street name that fits in thirty characters. The assumptions baked into a US-shaped form Start listing what a typical address form quietly requires: a numeric five-digit postcode, a state chosen from a fixed list, a street line under a certain length, a city with no accents. Now compare that with a UK postcode like SW1A 1AA , a Canadian one like M5V 2T6 , a Japanese address with a prefecture and no street number, or a German street name with an umlaut.
articles.author: qinjie xu

articles.excerpt: If you have ever uploaded a paperback cover or illustrated interior to IngramSpark (or Lightning Source / DriveThruRPG) without owning a paid subscription to Adobe Acrobat Pro or InDesign, you have al…
articles.body: If you have ever uploaded a paperback cover or illustrated interior to IngramSpark (or Lightning Source / DriveThruRPG) without owning a paid subscription to Adobe Acrobat Pro or InDesign, you have almost certainly run into one of these automated preflight rejection notices: "PDF contains ICC color profiles" "Document contains transparency — flatten before submitting" "Total Ink Coverage (TAC) exceeds 240%" "Fonts are not embedded" What makes these rejections frustrating is that design apps like Canva Pro ("CMYK Print PDF") , Microsoft Word , and even default Affinity Publisher presets say "Print Ready" right on the export button—yet still violate ISO 15930-1 ( PDF/X-1a:2001 ) .

articles.title: I scraped my own dataset and fed it to my AI dashboard generator -- here's what it got right and wrong
articles.excerpt: I've been building DashPrompts, a tool that turns a CSV + a plain-English prompt into a real Power BI project. A fair question for any tool like this: does it actually work on data it's never seen, or…
articles.body: I've been building DashPrompts, a tool that turns a CSV + a plain-English prompt into a real Power BI project. A fair question for any tool like this: does it actually work on data it's never seen, or just the polished demo sets? So I scraped 52 real events off Dubai's own 30x30 fitness challenge listings -- title, location, category, event type, price, dates. Data was kept raw as is for the demo. Then I gave it this prompt: Build a dashboard with a blue and green color theme (DP World 30x30 Dubai brand). KPI cards for total events, number of categories, and number of locations. A bar chart of event count by category. A second bar chart of event count by event type. A detail table with title, location, category, event type, price, and dates. A slicer for location.

articles.title: How I Built a Safety Gate for My API Security Scanner – API-Gapwolf
articles.excerpt: Introduction I recently completed V1 of API-Gapwolf, a local-first API security scanner designed to identify potential security weaknesses in web APIs. It performs automated security checks, displays…
articles.body: Introduction I recently completed V1 of API-Gapwolf, a local-first API security scanner designed to identify potential security weaknesses in web APIs. It performs automated security checks, displays findings in a dashboard, stores scan history and generates PDF reports with sensitive information masked. How Does It Work? One of the important features of API-Gapwolf is its Safety Gate. Before sending a scan request, it checks: Permission confirmation. URL and target validation. Approved scanning scope. DNS pinning and private IP blocking. Request limits (100 requests). Redirect validation. Scan cancellation status. These controls help prevent unauthorized scanning, SSRF risks and unnecessary traffic to target APIs. What's Included in V1? 24 automated security checks across five families.

articles.title: How Do You Introduce DevOps Practices to a Team That's Never Used Them?
articles.excerpt: Introducing continuous integration, continuous delivery, and automation to an inexperienced engineering team is primarily an exercise in change management rather than a tooling upgrade. Leaders often…
articles.body: Introducing continuous integration, continuous delivery, and automation to an inexperienced engineering team is primarily an exercise in change management rather than a tooling upgrade. Leaders often stumble by procuring modern cloud platforms and demanding immediate compliance, which creates friction, anxiety, and silent workarounds. Success comes from targeting developer friction, building psychological safety, and automating one highly visible bottleneck before layering on more complex infrastructure. Start by mapping the current deployment cycle alongside the engineers who run it manually. Identify the single most tedious task, such as manual artifact packaging or ad hoc database migrations, and replace it with a consistent script running on an isolated pipeline.

articles.title: 12 grains of dust found high in Earth's atmosphere reveal secrets of water at the edge of the solar system
articles.excerpt: Grains of dust found floating in Earth's stratosphere hold the secrets of a special kind of 'heavy' water that seems to be abundant in the outer solar system.
articles.body: A dozen grains of dust that have wandered in from the distant Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune were found floating in Earth's stratosphere. And it turns out they hold the secrets of a special kind of 'heavy' water that seems to be surprisingly abundant in the outer solar system. When analyzed by a team of scientists the 12 dust grains, which were captured by NASA's stratospheric ER-2 research aircraft, show signs of having interacted with a form of water that contains heavy oxygen isotopes. This is important because to better understand how the planets formed, scientists are seeking to understand how various materials were distributed around the early solar system 4.5 billion years ago.
